title: Challenge and appeal hooks
canonical_definition: Integrate verifier decisions with dispute holds and later stake/slash adjudication.
user_shorthand: Connect disputed results to the dispute layer.

roadmap_order.note: CMP-1.4.4 remains open. CMP-1.4.9 preserves and projects the original recorded verification tuple; it does not claim the still-open canonical signed-verdict binding work is complete.

implementation.original_decision_rule: Challenge/appeal state stores and returns the original verificationRef, resultCommitment, verifier and verification-policy tuple; no hook rewrites the original verdict.
implementation.chronology_rule: Review exposes grounds/evidence, response, first decision, appeal, appeal decision, adjudicators, deadlines, resolution and case status from the authoritative dispute case.
implementation.hold_rule: holdActive is true only for OPEN, RESPONDED, DECIDED and APPEALED cases and false after FINAL, WITHDRAWN or TIMED_OUT.
implementation.later_adjudication_rule: adverseToOriginalVerification is true only after a final disposition adverse to the originally approved result. It is a candidate signal only; a future stake/slash layer must independently validate policy, objective evidence, actor/subject and slash authorization.

authority_boundaries: Challenge/appeal hooks are read-only projections and cannot alter the original verificationRef/result/verifier/policy tuple.
The authoritative dispute engine, not the hook, owns case state, deadlines, claimant/respondent roles and adjudicator independence.
An unresolved challenge retains the existing contested-entitlement hold and cannot authorize provider release.
A challenge, appeal, or adverse final disposition does not itself move Vault funds; economic effects continue through the already-qualified entitlement/dispute resolution path.
adverseToOriginalVerification is not proof of verifier fault and grants no slash, stake, custody, settlement, governance, bridge, validator, worker or wallet authority.
Later stake/slash adjudication must independently validate exact bound policy and objective evidence and cannot punish solely from an allegation or nonfinal case.
Withdrawal/provider-win finality is not represented as an adverse verifier disposition.
Private evidence bytes remain off-chain; hooks expose bounded commitments and chronology only.

milestone_relationship.rationale: CMP-1.4.9 connects verifier provenance to the shared dispute/entitlement lifecycle. The retained Compute suite must revalidate dispute holds, appeal finality, payer/provider economic isolation and verifier-method behavior together.

exit_criteria: A verifier-facing review hook exposes the original verification identity/result/policy plus authoritative challenge and appeal chronology.
A job-scoped hook exposes whether the original verification is currently under a dispute hold.
The original verification tuple remains immutable through challenge, decision, appeal and finality.
OPEN/RESPONDED/DECIDED/APPEALED cases remain held; FINAL/WITHDRAWN/TIMED_OUT cases are not held.
A final payer-adverse-to-provider disposition can be identified as a later verifier-adjudication candidate without authorizing slashing.
Withdrawal/provider-win finality is not mislabeled as verifier fault.
Hooks do not move funds, rewrite verdicts or grant stake/slash/custody/settlement authority.
Focused challenge/appeal tests and retained Compute dispute/economic tests pass.
Level 1 and the CMP-1.4 verifier-dispute lifecycle Level 2 integration suite are green on the same exact implementation SHA.
completion_note: Exact-head Level 1 and CMP-1.4 verifier-dispute lifecycle Level 2 qualification passed on c125a25ab070ea5511d50e82045ae9b96ddadbb3. This closeout update is evidence-only and changes no executable source, tests, workflows, dependencies, interfaces, deployment state, or substantive requirements.
